main_text.p: lixe nos alibi demonstrauimus, ipsum, alios-que, qui similia tradunt, loqui pugnantia. Sed in re tam clara quid Græca cum Romana teneat, inuestigemus; vt discat Hottingerus verum a falso discernere. Niceta Byzantius pro Concilio Chalcedonensi contra Armeniæ Principem, Οʹπ ὁ καλῶς φρονῶν τὸ μικρὸν, κατ' ὀλίγον [?]πισπάτω. πᾶν ἢ τὸ εἰς [?]πίστιν ἀπόρον, καὶ [?]πίστων ἀπὸ Θεοῦ, μίσους, καὶ ὑποστροφῆς ἄξιον. Qui parum negligit, paulatim cadit; quodcunque vero in casum adducit, & casum a Deo, execrationis, auersionisque dignum est. Nec aliud sonant verba Eulogij Alexandrini; Ἐʼπὶς τῆς ἀκουώντων τοῖς θεοφόροις [?]παῤῥήσιας ἐχαλῶν, ἐπὶ τῆς οἰκουμένης κλητέον, ἀλλὰ ἀμφιβαίην, καὶ [?]θεοσέβειας δόγματος, καὶ περὶ τὸ θεῖον ἀσέβειαν. Ex illis, quæ diuini Patres approbarunt, aliquid præuertere, nullo modo dispositio appellanda est, sed prævaricatio, & proditio dogmatis, & circa res diuinas impietas. Diuersum itaque dogma diuersitatem fidei generat: potest tamen diuersos ritus sub vna fide vnitatem Ecclesiæ conseruare. Irenæus lib. 5. cap. 21. cum varias ieiuniorum formas enumerasset. Καὶ ὑδὲν ἔλαττον πάντες ἔτοι ἀφλωδοσάν τε καὶ ἐφλωδοσάμων θεὸς ἀλλήλως, καὶ ἡ διαφωνία τῆς νηστείας τῷ ὁμόνοιαν τῆς πίστεως συνίσησαν.

page.notes: The Greek in this page is set in a small, worn type. Words marked [?] are my best reading and should be checked against the scan. The first Greek line ("Οʹπ ὁ καλῶς φρονῶν…") and the Greek of the Eulogius quotation, and the Greek of the Irenaeus passage, are the least certain. The Irenaeus Greek line is partly illegible in places and may contain printing errors; I have left the printed forms as they appear. The top edge of the page is cut, so the first line may be missing its first letters. The left edge shows show-through and a dark border, which I have not transcribed.
